Line Fitting & Curve Fitting

Given a few data points, can you predict what comes next? You'll start with a simple question, discover the formula hiding in the data, and build your way to fitting lines and curves to anything.

Part 1: The Prediction Problem~15 min

There's a mystery box. You feed it a number x and it gives back a number y. You tried it twice:

xy
13
27
xy
13
27
3?11
2.5?9
2.1?7.4
0?−1
0.5?1
x1?4x1 − 1

How much will y be when x = 3?

✓ y = 11! When x goes up by 1, y goes up by 4.

How much when x = 2.5?

✓ y = 9! Half a step in x → half the increase.

What about x = 2.1?

✓ y = 7.4! Just 0.1 past x = 2, so 7 + 0.4.

Now try x = 0.

✓ y = −1! Going back from x = 1 subtracts 4.

What about x = 0.5?

✓ y = 1! Halfway between −1 and 3.

For any x1, can you write y = ?

y = 4x − 1

You just discovered a linear function!

You started with two data points and a guess. You ended with functions that fit lines and curves to any data — and a way to measure which fit is better. This is the foundation of regression, one of the most important tools in machine learning.

Going further:

  • More features: What if y depends on two inputs (x₁ and x₂)? That's multiple linear regression — same idea, more dimensions.
  • Gradient descent: For complex models, solving for the best parameters directly gets hard. Gradient descent finds them iteratively — see the Gradient Descent chapter on this site.
  • Overfitting: A high-degree polynomial fits your data perfectly but predicts terribly on new data. How do you know when you've gone too far?

Glossary

Slope (m)
How much y changes when x increases by 1 — the steepness of the line.
Intercept (c)
The value of y when x = 0 — where the line crosses the y-axis.
Linear function
A function of the form y = mx + c — it draws a straight line.
Residual
The difference between an actual y value and the predicted y value.
Mean Squared Error (MSE)
The average of the squared residuals — measures how well a model fits the data.
Polynomial
A function like y = ax² + bx + c — uses powers of x to fit curves.
Overfitting
Using too many parameters so the model memorizes the data instead of learning the pattern.
